title: Choose starting-state and prove reset deliberately
when: Before scheduling QA that resets a host
need: A dedicated baseline needs golden capture plus restore proof, not just SSH or a saved archive. Verify/reset are destructive provisioning operations. No baseline is also a supported no-reset posture; an as_is case needs a reason. Capacity-machine registration is separate from test-machine registration. A nonzero native baseline probe retains its diagnosed quota, authentication, model or transport cause. Quota and unknown failures preserve the golden and do not justify sign-in or credential resets; authentication recovery needs actual native evidence. Linux reset must keep desktop Chromium sign-ins live outside goldens, preserve ~/snap/chromium/common/chromium only when present, never restore stale sign-in state from an older golden, and stop Chromium before preservation to flush its state. Require separate real reset and browser sign-in proof against the selected release.
surface: Per-OS capture/verify/reset; machine setting optional baseline; Pack starting-state contract. Current Linux golden-home reference and Machine QA Linux baseline capture/recovery procedure.
gap: The entry guide must explain when a resettable rig is necessary. Do not make every browser user build a clean-install lab or mistake capacity registration for QA readiness.
review: Pending exact recipe proof. The Linux snap-store rule is operator-required candidate teaching. The exact producer correction and its source checks, real reset/sign-in proof and released delivery remain pending; current observed harness-store behavior does not prove this browser-store requirement.
